_about: One playbook per problem type: what facts to collect, what proof matters, the escalation ladder, and when to hand over to a real lawyer. Keywords are used by code (not the model) to pick which law cards go into the prompt.

deposit.label: Security deposit not returned by landlord
facts_to_collect: city and state
rent and deposit amount
date you moved in and date you vacated / handed over keys
is there a written rent agreement, and what does it say about deposit and deductions
what the landlord says the deductions are for
how the deposit was paid (bank/UPI/cash)
ladder: Ask in writing (WhatsApp/email) for the refund with a deadline of 7-15 days and ask for an itemised list of deductions
Send a legal notice (Nyay Saathi can draft it) by Speed Post/Registered Post AD and keep the receipt
Try free settlement through the DLSA / Lok Adalat
File for recovery before the Rent Authority (if your state has one) or the civil court
lawyer_when: landlord claims large damages or files a counter-claim
amount is large (over ~Rs 5 lakh)
you need to file the civil suit itself

consumer.label: Refund / defective product / bad service (consumer)
facts_to_collect: what was bought, from whom (platform + seller), price and date
what went wrong and when
what the company said (complaint/ticket numbers)
what you want: refund, replacement or compensation
ladder: Complain to the company's grievance officer in writing and note the ticket number
Register on the National Consumer Helpline (1915 / consumerhelpline.gov.in)
Optional: send a legal notice (helps, but not legally required for a consumer complaint)
File a consumer complaint on e-Jagriti (free up to Rs 5 lakh paid)
lawyer_when: the claim involves injury, medical negligence or a builder/real-estate matter
the company has already filed something against you
value paid above Rs 50 lakh

salary.label: Salary / wages not paid
facts_to_collect: employer name and city
your role and monthly salary
which months are unpaid and total amount
are you still working, or did you resign / get removed (date)
offer letter / appointment letter, payslips, bank statements
how many co-workers are in the same situation
ladder: Write to HR/employer by email asking for payment by a date
Send a legal notice
File a wage claim with the Labour Department authority under the Code on Wages (s.45) - can be a joint claim with co-workers
Civil suit (mainly for senior managerial roles - take a lawyer's advice)
lawyer_when: you are in a senior managerial role
the employer has threatened or filed a case against you
the company is shutting down / insolvency

cheque.label: Cheque bounce (giving or receiving a notice)
facts_to_collect: are you the person who GAVE the cheque or who RECEIVED it
cheque amount and date
date the bank returned it and the reason on the return memo
date the notice was sent / received
what the money was for
proof: proof of the underlying debt (agreement, chats, invoices)
ladder: If you RECEIVED a bounced cheque: send the demand notice within 30 days of the return memo
Wait 15 days from when the notice is received
File the complaint within the next one month
If you GAVE the cheque and got a notice: the 15-day window matters - paying within it avoids the offence; get legal advice immediately
lawyer_when: you received a court summons
you dispute that you owe the money
the 15-day or one-month deadline is close or has passed

domestic.label: Domestic violence / cruelty by husband or in-laws
facts_to_collect: is she safe right now, and where is she living now (matrimonial home / parents' home / elsewhere)
who did it (husband, in-laws) and since when; the latest incident date
injuries: was she treated, is there a hospital/medical (MLC) record, are the scars on face or head
any dowry or money demands
children: their ages and who they are with
her income and the husband's income (for maintenance)
has any police complaint, FIR or court case already been filed by either side
city and state
proof: medical / MLC report from a government hospital (get one now even for old injuries; the doctor records the scars)
dated photos of injuries and scars
WhatsApp/SMS/voice notes with threats or dowry demands
names of neighbours or relatives who saw or heard it
list of stridhan and jewellery given at marriage, with photos or bills
copies of any earlier police complaint or NCR
ladder: SAFETY FIRST: if in danger now, call 112, or 181 (Women Helpline), which connects to the district One Stop Centre for free medical help, police help, a lawyer and shelter
Get a medical examination at a government hospital and ask for a medico-legal (MLC) report recording every injury and scar; photograph the injuries
Meet the district Protection Officer (via 181, the One Stop Centre or the DLSA) and record a Domestic Incident Report

File the DV Act application (s.12) before the Magistrate where she now lives, asking for an urgent ex parte protection order, residence order, monetary relief/maintenance, custody and compensation (Nyay Saathi can draft it)
Criminal route (her choice, can run in parallel): written police complaint/FIR for cruelty and hurt at any police station (Zero FIR); if refused, send it to the SP (Nyay Saathi can draft it)
Free lawyer from the DLSA (15100); women get free legal aid regardless of income
lawyer_when: for the court hearings a free DLSA lawyer can represent her - mention this once, after the plan, not instead of it
the husband has filed or threatens divorce, custody or a false case
there are children and custody is disputed
injuries are serious or there are threats to life (also call 112)
must_cover: Safety today: if she cannot stay safely tonight, the One Stop Centre (via 181) gives free shelter; 112 if in danger now
The two legal routes and which to start with: (1) DV Act case for fast protection, home and money; (2) police complaint for punishment. They can run together; your recommendation and why
Urgent protection: the Magistrate can pass an ex parte protection order on her affidavit, first hearing ordinarily within 3 days
Her home: she cannot be thrown out of the matrimonial home; if she leaves for safety, she can still file where she then lives (e.g. her parents' town)
Money: medical costs, monthly maintenance, compensation for injuries and mental torture, and return of her stridhan
Evidence to secure TODAY: MLC from a government hospital, dated photos, messages/voice notes, witnesses, stridhan list; keep copies OUTSIDE the house (trusted person or cloud)

Criminal side in specifics: dowry cruelty and hurt/grievous hurt (scars on the face can be grievous hurt; the medical report decides); FIR at any police station; if refused, write to the SP; be honest that a cruelty-only complaint may first go to a Family Welfare Committee for 2 months
What the husband's side may do (pressure to compromise, counter-allegations, throw her out, hide stridhan) and how to guard against it
End with the 1-3 questions that change the plan most: children? a safe place to stay? any complaint already filed?

threats.label: Threats, blackmail or extortion (including online)
facts_to_collect: who is threatening you, how you know them and since when
exactly what they threaten to do (publish photos or chats, harm you, a false case, tell family or employer), in their own words if possible
what they demand (amount or act) and by when
the date of each threat or demand, and the channel (WhatsApp number, Instagram or other handle, calls, in person)
whether you have paid anything already: amount, date, mode (UPI or bank reference)
whether anything has already been posted or sent to anyone
what evidence you have and where it is (screenshots, chat export, call recordings on your phone)
whether you have complained to the police or on cybercrime.gov.in
whether you are a woman (some offences, like stalking and voyeurism, protect women) and whether anyone involved is under 18
proof: screenshots that show the sender's number or handle and the date and time
full chat export with media; keep the original phone and do not delete or edit the chat
call recordings and call logs (original files on the phone)
UPI or bank statements for any money paid
links (URLs) and screenshots of anything posted
acknowledgement numbers of any police or cybercrime complaint
ladder: Do not pay more and do not delete anything; stop engaging beyond what is necessary
Preserve evidence: export chats with media, note numbers, handles and URLs, keep the original phone safe
If intimate images are posted or threatened, complain to the platform (24-hour takedown) and on cybercrime.gov.in
File a police complaint or e-FIR at any police station; extortion is a cognizable offence
A legal notice (cease-and-desist) is optional and never a pre-condition for a police complaint; it suits cases where the person is identified and a written record and undertaking would help
Civil remedies (an injunction against publication, damages) go through a lawyer
lawyer_when: you or the other person is under 18
intimate images are already published and you need a court takedown order
you have been threatened with death or physical harm
a false case has been filed or threatened against you
you want a civil injunction or damages

other.label: Something else
facts_to_collect: what happened, when, who is involved, what you want
ladder: Take the facts first: ask the 3-5 questions a lawyer would ask, explain in plain words how this kind of matter generally works, the usual options (talk, written notice, mediation, legal aid, police or court) and what documents to collect. Don't cite sections that are not on a card.
After the facts are clear, if it still falls outside the 5 covered types, say a lawyer is needed, give the specific reason, and point to free legal aid (15100 / DLSA).
lawyer_when: after the facts are collected, for problems outside the 5 covered types

red_flags.message: If someone has been arrested, or a case, summons or warrant is against you, time matters: you have the right to a lawyer, and a free one is available - NALSA 15100 or your District Legal Services Authority. Don't sign or admit anything until you have read it and taken advice.
red_flags._note: 'not_when': phrases where the arrest or case is aimed at the OTHER side ('get him arrested'); they are removed before matching, so a client who wants to complain is not told a case is against them.

red_flags.message: If she is in danger right now: call 112. Women Helpline 181 (free, 24x7) connects to the district One Stop Centre: free medical exam, police help, a lawyer and shelter.
I'm really sorry you're going through this. Please talk to someone now: Tele-MANAS 14416 (free, 24x7) or 112 in an emergency.
If money was taken through online fraud, call 1930 or report at cybercrime.gov.in immediately - acting within hours improves the chance of freezing the money.

Divorce, custody, land and inheritance matters usually end up needing a lawyer to file in court - but first take the client's facts, explain in plain words how such a matter generally works, and what to collect and ask.
